evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Jasper Dekoninck, Mark Niklas Müller and Martin Vechev

receipt.public_excerpt: However, data contamination can lead to inflated performance, rendering them unreliable for model comparison.

evidence_items.explanation: ConStat reports contamination findings across several popular models and distinguishes inflated scores from generalizing performance. These earlier results establish a real failure mechanism, but not its frequency in the target period.

receipt.public_excerpt: This paper presents an interdisciplinary meta-review of about 100 studies that discuss shortcomings in quantitative benchmarking practices, published in the last 10 years.

evidence_items.explanation: The review documents recurring concerns including gaming, contamination and weak links between tests and the capabilities they purport to measure. Its selection of studies about shortcomings does not measure how often benchmark improvements fail to reflect real progress.

receipt.public_excerpt: Furthermore, frontier AI time horizon has been doubling approximately every seven months since 2019, though the trend may have accelerated in 2024.

evidence_items.explanation: This evaluation connects improvement to the duration of tasks measured against human performance, showing that benchmarks can provide interpretable evidence of capability gains. It does not establish the reliability of benchmarks generally, and the authors qualify transfer to real-world work.

unresolved_gaps: The evidence establishes real vulnerabilities but does not settle their prevalence across commonly used benchmarks during the target period.
No sufficiently broad matched comparison was found between reported benchmark gains and independent relevant task gains.
